radiusSource: Radius 1.258 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract): 875,191 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.204 +/- 0.052 solar masses from Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6354 +/- 70 K from Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hr-858.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.319, rounded to two decimals
